spec_cite: docs/wire-protocol-v2/spec.md §3 (framing: length == 0 or > 65536 -> 401; 64 KiB is the cap, not 64 KiB − 1)
description: Boundary: a frame whose length is EXACTLY 65536 passes the framing check (only > 65536 violates) and is processed — here a Subscribe plus an unknown padding field, answered with SubscribeResponse(OK).
preconditions: The body is Subscribe{request_id=1} followed by unknown field 1000 carrying 65519 zero bytes — the unknown field is ignored under the standard evolution rule (§4.4).

No message type in v2.0 naturally fills 64 KiB (detail caps at 256 B), so the padding pins the pure framing boundary; a length of 65537 (see control.error-401-frame-length-oversize) must fail ON THE PREFIX, before allocation.
assertions: The framing check is purely length-based: 65536 is accepted, 65537 is refused before allocation (§3).
The unknown field is ignored; the Subscribe inside is processed normally.
Any receiver that 401s a valid 65536-byte frame, or buffers a 65537-byte one before checking, violates the spec.
